chunks: My father narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Talha ibn Zayd. He said: I heard Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) say:
One who acts without insight is like one who travels without a path, and increasing his speed in travel only increases his distance from the path.

key_terms.السَّائِر: al-sa'ir — the traveler, the one walking or journeying
key_terms.الْعَامِل: al-'amil — the one who acts or works; here referring to one who performs religious or moral deeds
key_terms.بَصِيرَة: basira — insight, discernment, inner vision; the capacity to perceive religious truth clearly

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about acting without insight or knowledge?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) presents a vivid analogy: acting without insight (basira) is like travelling without a road — the faster one moves, the further one strays. This teaching was addressed to Shia Muslims who needed guidance on grounding their deeds in sound religious knowledge and discernment, not mere zeal or blind imitation. The term 'basira' in classical usage denotes inner spiritual vision and knowledge of what is right — acting without it leads not just to error, but to compounding error.

en.bilal-muhammad: My father narrated to us. He said: Sa`d b. `Abdullah narrated to us from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Khalid from his father from Muhammad b. Sinan from Talha b. Zayd. He said: I heard Aba `Abdillah al-Sadiq (as) say:
One who acts without insight is like one who travels without a path. If he increases his speed in his travel, he only gets further away from the path.
